## Upgrading from v0.8.x

**`LifterBuilder::home`, `script` and `intermediate_dir` take the value itself, not an `Option`.** Leave a setting out by not calling its method, which keeps the default as before.

```rust
// before
LifterBuilder::new(ir).home(Some(PathBuf::from("/opt/ghidra"))).script(None)
// now
LifterBuilder::new(ir).home("/opt/ghidra")
```

## Highlights

- **`info` lists the pairing strategies and the aggregators** as well as the birthmarks and the algorithms, so that every name `compare` and `run` take can be looked up in one place.
- **TF-IDF weighting, as a script** (#207). `assets/scripts/tfidf.py INPUT_DIR OUTPUT_DIR` reads `op-seq`, `op-freq`, `fc-seq`, `fc-freq`, `op-{k}gram-seq` or `op-{k}gram-freq` birthmarks and writes each as the matching frequency birthmark, its counts weighted by how rare each element is among the functions of all the inputs, so that an element nearly every function has counts for little. The outputs are ordinary frequency birthmarks: `compare` reads them under every frequency algorithm, and only birthmarks converted together are comparable with each other. The IDF table they came from is written to `OUTPUT_DIR/idf.csv`.
- **Each release carries `oinkie-X.Y.Z_checksums.txt`** (#205), the SHA-256 of all six archives in the format `sha256sum -c` reads, so that a download can be checked and a packaging script can pin the hash it expects. [Installation](https://tamada.github.io/oinkie/install/) shows how to check one on Linux, macOS and Windows.
- **`Extractor::new` takes anything that converts into a `BirthmarkType`**: a `BirthmarkType` as before, a `&BirthmarkType`, or an `AnalysisType` or `&AnalysisType`, whose birthmark it extracts. `Extractor::new(&analysis)` replaces `Extractor::new(analysis.birthmark().clone())`, and code that passed a `BirthmarkType` compiles unchanged.
- **Paths and strings are taken as they come.** `Program::load` and the new `Birthmark::load` take anything that is a path, so `Program::load("a.json")` replaces `Program::load(Path::new("a.json"))`; `set_json_path` on both takes anything that converts into a `PathBuf`, and `Kgram::new` any sequence of strings. Code that passed the old types compiles unchanged.
